## Script Summary 
This script relies on `02_PanCancer-RenderReport-miRNA.Rmd` to provide input (TCGA project to perform analysis on) and covariates
that were dynamically determined as part of meta data harmonization. 

This script: 

- Utilizes processed SummarizedExperiment miRNA RDS file

- Performs differential expression analysis using `DESeq2` to 
identify miRNA whose expression is associated with age, with provided covariates


```{r file paths}
se_directory <- file.path(TCGA, "miR/processed_data/all/")

output_dir_dge <- file.path(PATH,"results/mirna/DE_analysis/")
```


## Data Loading
Here we load in the filtered miRNA SummarizedExperiment object. 
```{r Load in se object}
#Summarized Experiment
se <- readRDS(paste0(se_directory,selected_cancer_type,"_miRNA.rds"))
```


```{r}
print(paste0("Running differential analysis for ", selected_cancer_type ))
```


```{r, include = FALSE}
create_reactable_table <- function(se, covariate_name) {
  if (!is.null(colData(se)[[covariate_name]])) {
    # Generate frequency table
    freq_table <- table(colData(se)[[covariate_name]])
    
    # Convert to data frame for reactable
    df <- as.data.frame(freq_table)
    names(df) <- c(covariate_name, "Count")
    
    # Create reactable
    reactable::reactable(df, highlight = TRUE)
  } else {
    cat(paste0("Covariate '", covariate_name, "' not found.\n"))
  }
}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
reactable_pretty <- function(results) {
 results <- results %>% mutate(across(where(~is.numeric(.) && any(. %% 1 != 0, na.rm = TRUE)), ~signif(., digits = 3)))
 reactable::reactable(results,searchable = TRUE,resizable = TRUE)
}
```

## Differential Analysis: DESeq2
Here we use `DESeq2` to identify features whose expression is associated with age. 

## Covariate Prepartation 
We dynamically determine the covariates to include in a previous script ("metadata/scripts/05_Covariates.Rmd).
This script utilizes those covariates to create a design matrix for analysis with `DESeq2`.
```{r Prepare Covariates for Limma}
# Start with a basic model including only the age variable
model_formula <- "~ Age"

#Remove samples with missing age
se <- se[,!is.na(se$Age)]

# Include purity only if selected_cancer_type is not "TCGA-LAML"
if (include_purity) {
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ purity")
  # Remove samples with missing purity
  se <- se[, !is.na(se$purity)]
  }


# Dynamically add covariates and filter SE based on parameters
if (include_gender) {
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ gender")
  #Drop NA gender samples
  se <- se[,!is.na(se$gender)]
  create_reactable_table(se, "gender")
  }

if (include_race) {
  
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ race")
  #Drop NA race samples
  se <- se[,!is.na(se$race)]
  
  races_to_keep <- strsplit(as.character(races_to_include), ",\\s*")[[1]]
  #print(paste0("Only keeping samples in these racial categories: ", races_to_include))
  se <- se[, se$race %in% races_to_keep]
  create_reactable_table(se, "race")

}

if (include_subtype) {
  model_formula <- paste(model_formula, "+ subtype_selected")
  #Drop NA tumor subtypes samples
  se <- se[,!is.na(se$subtype_selected)]
  create_reactable_table(se, "subtype_selected")
}

if (include_hpv) {
    #drop HPV positive samples (should be for HNSC only as of now)
    se <- se[, !is.na(se$HPV.status) & se$HPV.status == "Negative"]
    create_reactable_table(se, "HPV.status")
}

# Convert model formula to a formula object
model_formula <- as.formula(model_formula)

# Print model being used in limma
# Here we use deparse to convert the formula to a string
model_formula_str <- deparse(model_formula)
paste0("Limma Model Formula: ", model_formula_str)
```


```{r}
# Prepare the design matrix 
design <- model.matrix(model_formula, data = colData(se))
head(unique(design))
```

```{r check-samples, echo=FALSE}
# Calculate the number of samples remaining
num_samples <- ncol(se)

# Print the number of samples
cat("Number of samples remaining after covariate filtering:", num_samples, "\n")

# Check if the number of samples is less than 50
if (num_samples < 50) {
  # Stop the R Markdown rendering with a custom message
  stop("Less than 50 samples remaining. Analysis requires 50 samples.")
}
```

## DEseq2
Here, we  perform differential gene expression analysis using the `DESeq2` package. Note that we do not need to apply explicit normalization, as this is handled internally by the `DESeq()` function: 

This function performs a default analysis through the steps:

- estimation of size factors: estimateSizeFactors

- estimation of dispersion: estimateDispersions

- Negative Binomial GLM fitting and Wald statistics: nbinomWaldTest

Some rows have missing p-values. Why? some values in the results table can be set to NA for one of the following reasons:

- If within a row, all samples have zero counts, the baseMean column will be zero, and the log2 fold change estimates, p value and adjusted p value will all be set to NA. 

- If a row contains a sample with an extreme count outlier then the p value and adjusted p value will be set to NA. These outlier counts are detected by Cook’s distance

- If a row is filtered by automatic independent filtering, for having a low mean normalized count, then only the adjusted p value will be set to NA. Description and customization of independent filtering is described below

### Run DESeq2
Here we run `DESeq` with the default parameters and created model formula. 
```{r deseq2 analysis}
print(model_formula)

# Extract the filtered counts
counts_filtered <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se,"raw_counts")

# Build the DESeq2 dataset object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts_filtered,
                              colData = colData(se),
                              design = model_formula)

# Run the DESeq2 pipeline
dds <- DESeq(dds, parallel = TRUE)
```

### Retrieve Results
Next, we retrieve our analysis results.

First, we retrieve our age-regression results including internal filtering by `DESeq2` using the `results()` function. This internal filtering essentially maximizes the number of significant differentially expressed genes by excluding some genes when calculating adjusted p-values. We utilize this report the number of significant DEGs for the cancer type. 
See more information here: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html#indfilt

Second, we retrieve the unfiltered results (results for ALL genes included in our analysis) with and without shrunken logFC values using the `DESeq2::lfcShrink()` function. 

We also save all versions of these results.
```{r}
# Get filtered results (default DESeq2 filtering)
results_filtered <- results(dds, name = "Age")  # Automatically applies independent filtering
results_filtered_df <- as.data.frame(results_filtered) %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj) & !is.na(log2FoldChange))  # Filter rows with missing values

# Save filtered, non-shrunken results
saveRDS(results_filtered_df, paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_filtered_DESeq2_results.rds"))
write.csv(results_filtered_df, gzfile(paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_filtered_DESeq2_results.csv.gz")))

# Save filtered, non-shrunken results
results_unfiltered <- results(dds, name = "Age", independentFiltering = FALSE)
saveRDS(results_unfiltered, paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_DESeq2_results.rds"))
write.csv(results_unfiltered, gzfile(paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_DESeq2_results.csv.gz")))

# Shrink log2 fold changes for unfiltered results
results_unfiltered_df <- as.data.frame(results_unfiltered)
results_shrunken <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "Age", type = "apeglm")
results_shrunken_df <- as.data.frame(results_shrunken)

# Save unfiltered, shrunken results
saveRDS(results_shrunken_df, paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_shrunken_DESeq2_results.rds"))
write.csv(results_shrunken_df, gzfile(paste0(output_dir_dge, selected_cancer_type, "_unfiltered_shrunken_DESeq2_results.csv.gz")))


# reactable of filtered results
reactable_pretty(as.data.frame(results_filtered_df))
```


### Summary Table
```{r summary deseq2}
# Summary Table for Filtered Results
summary_stats <- results_filtered_df %>%
  mutate(direction = ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0, "Up", "Down")) %>%
  summarise(
    Total = n(),
    Q_Value_0.05 = sum(padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q_Value_0.025 = sum(padj <= 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q_Value_0.01 = sum(padj <= 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    IncreasedExp_with_Age = sum(padj <= 0.05 & direction == "Up", na.rm = TRUE),
    DecreasedExp_with_Age = sum(padj <= 0.05 & direction == "Down", na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Print the summary table
reactable::reactable(summary_stats)
```

### Volcano Plot
This volcano plot visualizes the FILTERED results of our age-regression analysis with `DESeq2`.
```{r volc dseq2}
results_filtered_df$gene <- rownames(results_filtered_df)

min_diff <- 0  # Adjust this threshold as per your requirement
max_fdr <- 0.05
dat <- results_filtered_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate(gene_type = case_when(
    log2FoldChange >  min_diff & padj <= max_fdr ~ "up",
    log2FoldChange < -min_diff & padj <= max_fdr ~ "dn",
    .default = "ns"))


# Using dplyr to remove NAs from specific columns
dat_cleaned <- dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj) & !is.na(log2FoldChange))

# Now you can proceed with your plotting or further analysis
print(ggplot_volcano(
  dat = dat_cleaned,
  xaxis = "log2FoldChange",
  yaxis = "padj",
  gene_label = "gene",
  xlab = "log2FoldChange",
  title = "DESeq2 Volcano Plot",
  yintercept = max_fdr,
  xintercept = c(-min_diff, min_diff),
  sig_il_genes = TRUE,
  up_il_genes = TRUE,
  dn_il_genes = TRUE,
  top_n = 3
))
```
